summary: This sermon explores Paul's multi-dimensional view of salvation, focusing on the past tense aspect as part of a three-week series. Pastor Ryan argues that American evangelicalism has oversimplified salvation to a single past event, when Scripture presents it as past, present, and future realities that together form God's plan to restore rebellious humanity.
key_points: Salvation encompasses three tenses: past (we were saved), present (we are being saved), and future (we will be saved)
Past tense salvation itself has three layers: eternity past (God's plan before creation), earthly past (the Fall), and individual past (personal rebellion)
Salvation is like adoption: enemies brought into God's family, given legal status, parented into growth, and promised an inheritance
We are rebels who want God's possessions without His presence or preferences, yet He runs to us like the father to the prodigal son
Believers should not become bored with salvation's beauty but spend a lifetime meditating on its depth and mystery
big_idea: God's salvation is not merely a past transaction but a magnificent, multifaceted work where He brings His enemies into His family through Christ—a reality so profound it deserves lifelong meditation rather than theological reduction.
title: A SUMMER'S JOURNEY: Tenses of Salvation
